newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate leader throws support to arms pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate leader throws support to arms pact.

text.p: Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott said on Thursday he will support a treaty outlawing chemical weapons when the Senate votes on U.S. approval of the pact later in the day.

"I have decided to vote in support of the Senate giving its advise and consent of the Chemical Weapons Convention," Lott said in a Senate speech hours before the decisive vote, apparently handing Democratic President Bill Clinton the backing he needed for a major foreign policy victory.
"I urge the adoption and the ratification of this treaty," Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said as the Senate worked its way through a series of "killer" amendments backed by treaty opponents.

Approval of any would effectively block U.S. participation in a treaty already approved by more than 70 nations, but Lott's decision seemed sure to bring sufficient Republican support on board to ensure unencumbered approval. The first of four such amendments was rejected before he announced his stand.

Lott told the Senate he had struggled over the treaty and the fundamental question of whether the United States was better off with or without it. He said he would vote for the pact because "because I believe there will be real and lasting consequences to the United States if we do not ratify the (Chemical Weapons) Convention."

He said the credibility of commitments made by two presidents -- Republican George Bush and Clinton -- was at stake and he believed the United states was "marginally better off with the treaty than without it."
